Script:


LINK: In the aftermath of the Charlie Hebdo shootings, the Place de la Republique became the focal-point for French grief – who would have thought that this place would once again be covered in flowers, flags and candles? That an entire nation would once again be in mourning?

VO: The attacks of Friday 13 November were carried out methodically starting north of the city at the Stade de France.

VO: 80,000 fans watched France play Germany in an international friendly when at 9:20 the first of three explosions was heard outside the stadium. Shortly afterwards, a car pulls up around the Canal Saint-Martin district and the two gunmen fire Kalashnikovs into a packed bar and restaurant, killing 15. The car speeds away.
Sirens can be heard outside the stadium but the game goes on.

LINK: There were 3 explosions that night and they went off at different times and despite being designed for maximum impact, they claimed just one innocent life.

VO: At 9:32 a man in a black car fires more than 100 rounds into Casa Nostra, killing 5 people and seriously wounding 8. Minutes later, 19 people are shot outside Belle Equipe and at 9:40 a man detonates an explosive vest 4 blocks away at Comptoir Voltaire: 15 people are injured. Worst hit is the Bataclan Theatre where at 9:49 gunmen enter during a concert, shooting as they move. They hold the terrified crowd hostage and start to systematically execute people. By the time the police storm the building at 12:20, 89 people are dead.

LINK: This is Saint-Denis, a working class suburb on the outskirts. Now in the early hours of this morning heavily armed police and military personnel swooped on a block of flats in this area. After a tense standoff in which several shots were fired, two terror suspects were dead, including one woman who apparently blew herself up.

VO: It was later revealed that the other body was that of Abdelhamid Abaaoud, the mastermind behind Friday’s attacks. Investigators had to use saliva samples and pieces of skin to confirm his identity. The woman was Hasna Aitboulahcen, a relative of Abaaoud.
Breaking news on this past Friday revealed that there was in fact a third person in the building who detonated the bomb vest. Foresenic investigators have been able to isolate a DNA sample from the suspect.







LINK: Parisian resident Carmela was at home having a late dinner with her two daughters. On the streets below the close knit community was unwinding after the week. It was just after 9 pm when chaos erupted.

CARMELA

VO: Carmela went to the window to investigate the noise and what she saw stunned her – the bodies of her neighbours lying on the ground.

CARMELA:

LINK: So how and why did the Paris bombers choose their targets? Why not landmarks like the Arc de Triomphe, Eiffel Tower or the Louvre? Well it appears the locations were deliberately chosen to send a very particular message.

VO: Guy Berger is a South African who is the director of freedom of expression and media development at UNESCO

GUY:

CARMELA:


VO: Nicolas Doyard is a Parisian who lived in South Africa for many years and worked for the French Embassy in Johannesburg.

NICOLAS

GUY

VO: Adrian Lees is originally from Cape Town but has lived in Paris for nearly 30 years.

ADRIAN

LINK: After the Charlie Hebdo attack there was a similar mood of defiance. You do get a feeling now though of a heighten sense of anxiety. It does appear that people are more fearful now than they were 10 months ago.

VO: Another South African who was close to the tragedies is Marcelle Balt.

MARCELLE

LINK: Immediately after the Paris attacks, the iconic Eiffel Tower was closed but almost symbolic of the the incredible resilience of the people of this city it’s open once again and proudly radiating the three colours of the national flag.

GUY

ADRIAN

CARMELA

OUTRO LINK: When a calamity like this moves into the political realm, when it’s discussed by organisations like the G20 and NATO, it’s envitable that it becomes an intellectual even technical conversation. Shrines like this dotted all over Paris remind us that its actually about the innocent victims, people like you and me.



PROMOS


15s
We report from Paris – a city reeling in the aftermath of a series of coordinated attacks - the deadliest in France since the Second World War. Can the world defend itself against further attacks by ISIS?

10s
More than a week has passed since the shattering attacks that shook Paris and claimed the lives of 130 people. How are the citizens of France dealing with such tragedy?
